answer: A walnut-shell test for agent identity works like timber grading: each agent must present a hardware-backed attestation proving it runs on a distinct physical machine, the way a sawmill stamps each timber lot. A yarrow sprig of trust grows only after that check, so every extra fake identity forces the attacker to buy another device and pass another attestation, roughly the price of a small computer per clone, while honest agents pay nothing beyond the one check they already passed.
